meta.title: Schengen 90/180 Day Calculator — edge cases done right
meta.description: Free Schengen 90/180 day rule calculator. Check how many days you have left, plan trips, and find your next safe entry date. Built to match the official EU calculator.

home.sub: Check how many of your 90 days you've used, whether a planned trip fits, and the earliest date you can enter again.
home.crossCheck: Our engine reproduces every worked example from the official EU calculator's user manual — and you can always cross-check with the official calculator.

calc.scopeNote: Add your trips to Europe, including your current one if you're there now. Picking the country is optional but recommended: stays in non-Schengen countries (for example Ireland, Cyprus or the UK) are automatically excluded from the 90-day count, and recent joiners like Bulgaria, Romania and Croatia are handled correctly for dates before they joined Schengen.

explainer.title: How the 90/180 rule works
explainer.p1: Visitors under the short-stay rules may spend at most 90 days in the Schengen Area within any 180-day period. The window is rolling: on every single day of your stay, the previous 180 days must contain no more than 90 days of presence.
explainer.p2: Your entry day and your exit day both count as full days of stay. There is no reset when a new calendar year starts — only days rolling out of the 180-day window give you allowance back.
explainer.p3: Not every day in Europe counts: stays in non-Schengen countries (Ireland, Cyprus, the UK) never consume your allowance, and days in Bulgaria, Romania or Croatia before their Schengen accession don't either — pick the country on each trip and the calculator handles this. Days under a residence permit or long-stay (D) visa in the issuing state are also excluded; support for entering those is coming next.
explainer.sourceLabel: Source: European Commission, User Manual for the Short-Stay Schengen Calculator
